problem: Limits-to-Learning lower bound on population R2 when noise has a shared unit-level (donor/period) component, validated on ground truth
source: Chen, Kelly, Malamud, 'Limits To (Machine) Learning' (arXiv:2512.12735, Dec 2025). Assumption 1 (Sec 3) takes the noise eps_t iid and independent of signals and predictable component; the LLG lower bound R2* >= (R2_OOS + L)/(1+L) and its CLT (Thm 3) are derived under it. Stated gap (App. F, leave-for-future-research): the best feasible MSE needs estimation of Sigma_beta (the coefficient covariance), described as highly complex. The cluster-noise limitation is my reading of Assumption 1, not an author statement.
formulation: y_dj = f(x_dj) + eta_d + e_dj, donors d=1..G, spots j=1..n_d, eta_d a donor-level shift (depth/detection factor) invisible to x, e_dj iid. Predictor = ridge or kernel ridge fitted leave-donor-out. Target: a data-driven lower confidence bound for the population R2 of f (within-donor part) and a separate bound for the between-donor part, as a function of leave-donor-out R2 and a computable gap L_c that uses G (not n) where eta enters.
closest_prior: 6 queries (web_search x2, arXiv API x3, Crossref x1; Semantic Scholar failed with 429). The only LLG paper found is the original (iid noise). Variance-component / SNR inference under p>n exists (EigenPrism arXiv:1505.02097; HEDE arXiv:2406.11184; multivariate SNR inference arXiv:2506.10370; misspecified mixed-model analysis, Jiang et al. AoS 2016) and the digest already holds a two-level EigenPrism idea (Repr B) and an embedding-heritability idea (Repr F). Difference from those: the object is a bound computed from out-of-sample R2 with a tuned ridge, not a variance-component estimate. Residual risk: a mixed-model argument may already give the cluster version in a line; I could not confirm that nothing exists, search quality of the APIs was poor.

problem: Dense (non-sparse) reduced-rank ridge with many proxies: limiting factor-space recovery and prediction risk at p ~ n and p > n
source: Wan, Li, Lu, Song, 'Mining the Factor Zoo: Estimation of Latent Factor Models with Sufficient Proxies' (arXiv:2212.12845; J. Econometrics 2024), Discussion, fourth point: the penalised reduced-rank regression avoids a sparsity assumption because lasso behaves poorly with correlated proxies, but without sparsity the theory at p ~ T is stated to be generally challenging and left as an extension.
formulation: Y (n x q genes) = X B + E, rank(B)=r small, X (n x p embeddings) with general covariance, p/n -> gamma in (0,inf), q/n finite, ridge-regularised reduced-rank estimator B_hat(lambda, r). Quantities: limiting out-of-sample risk, alignment of the estimated r-dimensional response subspace with the true one, and optimal singular-value shrinkage.
closest_prior: 3 queries (web_search x3). Closest: Dobriban-Wager arXiv:1507.03003 (single response ridge, proportional regime); Kargin arXiv:1409.6779 (reduced-rank regression with p, q, N proportional but N>=p and unpenalised; singular-value laws and rank selection); Bing-Wegkamp arXiv:1704.02381 and Bunea-She-Wegkamp (rank selection); Mukherjee-Zhu 2011 reduced-rank ridge (method, no limit theory found). The digest PRANK verdict (mostly_taken) concerns rank selection under a donor nuisance factor and leave-group-out CV; this problem differs in that it targets the ridge p>n limit of factor-space recovery with proxies, not selection. Not found does not mean absent: ML-theory papers on multi-output or deep linear ridge may contain it.

problem: Joint forecast-calibration (Mincer-Zarnowitz) test across N targets with small T and a strong common factor in the forecast errors
source: Zhao, Ma, Feng, 'High dimensional alpha test ... Lq-norm' (arXiv:2603.29764, Sec 5): tests assume temporally independent observations, extension to dependent or conditional models left for future research; Chernov, Kelly, Malamud, Schwab (NBER w33565) extend GRS to N>T with ridge-regularised covariance (regressors common to all assets). In forecasting, Qu-Timmermann-Zhu panel/cross-sectional EPA tests handle small T but compare accuracy, not calibration. Stated gap about MZ with N>T is my synthesis, not a statement by those authors.
formulation: For targets g=1..N and periods d=1..T (T < N, e.g. T=15-25, N=50-343): y_gd = a_g + b_g yhat_gd + u_gd, with equation-specific regressors yhat_gd and u_gd = lambda_g F_d + v_gd. Test H0: a_g=0, b_g=1 for all g, and the sparse alternative (few miscalibrated g).
closest_prior: 4 queries (web_search x2, arXiv API x2 returned physics junk). Found no N>T joint MZ test. Nearby: Fosten-Gutknecht arXiv:2302.02747 (multivariate quantile MZ, G=4 series), Qu-Timmermann-Zhu cross-sectional comparison tests (rady.ucsd.edu), a paper on the incidental-parameters bias of the CD test (doi 10.1080/07350015.2021.1906687, authors not retrieved), Massacci et al. arXiv:2507.17599 randomised alpha test. Risk: Pesaran-Yamagata-type quadratic or max statistics for SUR with equation-specific regressors may already cover it; the digest holds Shift G (finite-K calibration-slope t-test) and Multi J (Clark-West) that overlap in spirit.

problem: SNR frontier of random-feature ridge when signal strength varies randomly across groups (donors/periods) and the penalty is chosen by leave-group-out CV
source: 'Is sophistication a panacea? The learning capacity of random feature models for financial forecasting' (arXiv:2610.27255, Oct 2026; authors not extracted). Sec on posterior drift: the SNR needed to beat the zero forecast is higher under drift w (fixed, e.g. w=0.7); the authors leave the conjectured universality of the SNR frontier across eigenfunction distributions open, and note tighter bounds are possible.
formulation: Groups d=1..G with group-specific SNR rho_d ~ Pi (random), training groups and a new test group; ridge/RF-ridge with penalty lambda. Define the frontier set {(rho, lambda): risk < zero-forecast risk} for the mixture and the minimum penalty that guards against the worst plausible test-group SNR.
closest_prior: 4 queries (web_search x2, arXiv API x2). The base frontier with a fixed drift parameter is in 2610.27255 itself. Optimal ridge under covariate shift: arXiv:2404.01233 (Optimal Ridge Regularization for Out-of-Distribution Prediction; authors not retrieved). Ridge with correlated samples and CV: Atanasov et al. arXiv:2408.04607 (already in the digest as the closest to Repr A/I). Feature-group ridge: sigma-Ridge arXiv:2010.15817 (groups of features, not of samples). I did not find random per-group SNR; but the digest Shift F and Repr A/I cover neighbouring ground, so overlap risk is high.

problem: Latent-regressor / generated-regressor correction when the measurement errors of several ML predictions share a common component and no validation labels exist
source: Canen and Enamorado, 'When Predictions Become Regressors' (arXiv:2608.02909, Aug 2026), limitation paragraph and Conclusion: the split-sample correction assumes errors uncorrelated across observations conditional on the input; correlations induced by unobservables are plausible; future work on more than two splits or multiple prediction models, nonlinear outcome models and more complex dependence. Also Battaglia et al. (arXiv:2402.15585): errors can be nonclassical, difficult to correct.
formulation: Downstream regression z_i = beta*theta_i + c_i, theta_i latent, K measurements w_ik = theta_i + u_ik with u_ik = s_i + v_ik, s_i a common component (ten encoders reading the same image), no labelled theta. Identify or bound beta.
closest_prior: 3 queries (web_search x1, arXiv API x2 junk). Split-indicator correction with independent errors: Jerzak et al. arXiv:2507.22218; ML-generated regressor inference: arXiv:2402.15585, arXiv:2608.02909, arXiv:2301.10643; errors-in-variables with multiple indicators is classical (Schennach-type identification, not retrieved here). The digest already holds triple-collocation items (Repr H, Shift D) and the PPI exclusion is adjacent. High overlap risk.

problem: Inference on forecaster alignment / IC with few periods (donors) and spatially dependent units within a period
source: Soleimani, 'Target alignment, dilution and forecast selection...' (arXiv:2609.26303, Sep 2026), Limitations bullets and results: bootstrap inference for the joint alignment test is oversized under the dependence in the first panel; a single horizon, six outer origins, procedures tuned on the evaluation data. Ding-Sun 2023 supplies IC asymptotics for large T.
formulation: Dates d=1..G (G=15-25), units j=1..n_d with spatial dependence, K forecasters; alignment a_dk = corr_j(forecast, target); test H0: max_k mean_d a_dk <= 0 and the marginal gain of adding forecaster K+1 (improvement vs dilution).
closest_prior: 4 queries (web_search x2, arXiv API x2 junk). Within-date spatial correction exists since 1989 (Clifford-Richardson-Hemon, PubMed 2720048; Dutilleul 1993); IC asymptotics: Ding-Sun 2023 (J. Asset Management); small-T cross-sectional accuracy tests: Qu-Timmermann-Zhu; the digest BENCH (mostly_taken), Forecast F/H, Multi E and the SIGN item cover the across-donor part. Essentially a recombination of published pieces.
